title: Soft preemption latency-compromise design jam
content:
Purpose: rapid sync to land a working design for a "soft preemption" flow that balances tenant fairness and our tail-latency SLOs. This is a design-jam — not final RFC. We sketched tradeoffs and proposed a minimal rollout path that buys safety while data is collected.

Context / problem statement:
- On Dedicated/Dedicated-like pools with mixed tenant priorities we need to reclaim slots for higher-priority workload without causing large tail latency spikes or losing conversation state.
- Hard preemption (kill+restart) minimizes reclaim latency but blows up client-observed tails and loses KV cache, leading to repeated cold-start costs and quality regressions.
- Fully gentle draining (wait-for-idle) preserves user experience but can starve high-priority bursts and violates strict capacity guarantees.

High-level proposal (hybrid soft-preempt flow):
1) Preemption hint + priority check: scheduler emits a "soft-preempt" hint to the node indicating target slot(s) and reclaim urgency (urgent|normal|low). Hint includes tenant id, requester priority, and desired reclaim time horizon.
2) Grace window + windowed draining: Node attempts to finish in-flight token generation within a configurable grace window (default 2s for urgent, 10s for normal). If generator is in a batching window, we try to close the window early and issue partial response flush.
3) Snapshot checkpointing: If an active session holds >X MB of KV cache or is mid-conversation longer than N tokens, we attempt an asynchronous snapshot of minimal resume state to hotstore (per-tenant encrypted). Snapshot isn't a full model state — just enough to reconstruct KV cache pointers and tokenizer position.
4) Cache handoff / warming hint: For reclaimed slots, we emit a cache-warm hint to nearby nodes and mark the session as "warm-candidate" for a short TTL (default 2m) so subsequent requests prefer warm nodes. Hotstore keeps short-lived cache blobs keyed by session id.
5) Forced preempt fallback: If grace window expires and reclaim still required, node performs fast preemption with best-effort flush (settings determine whether to allow partial outputs to return to caller or to abort).

Key tradeoffs discussed:
- Grace window length: short windows reduce reclaim latency but increase partial responses and cache loss. Longer windows preserve UX but can cause SLA misses for higher-priority tenants. We agreed to start with conservative defaults and iterate with telemetry.
- Checkpoint frequency vs overhead: frequent checkpointing adds network and hotstore load; infrequent checkpointing raises the chance of full cache loss. Proposed heuristic: checkpoint only when session KV > 8MB or when a preemption hint arrives and session age > 30s.
- Security and privacy: snapshots written to hotstore must be tenant-scoped and encrypted with customer keys when configured. Need a review with platform secrets/KMS team.
- Determinism and correctness: resume logic must gracefully handle partial KV mismatches — fallback is to do a cold resume. Conversation sequence numbers should be used to detect divergence.

Telemetry and SLOs to track pre-rollout:
- preemption_request_rate (per pool, per priority)
- preemption_success_time_ms (time from hint to reclaimed slot)
- preemption_tail_rt_p95/p99 (requests impacted by preemption)
- resumed_sessions_ratio (fraction of sessions resumed from snapshot vs cold restart)
- hotstore_snapshot_success_rate and latency
- user-visible partial_response_rate (cases where partial outputs were returned due to early flush)

Acceptance criteria for gradual rollout (gate conditions):
- No >2x increase in p99 tail latency for baseline traffic in canary pool over 48h.
- snapshot_success_rate >= 99% and resume_success_rate >= 98% in canary.
- Preemption reclaim time for urgent priority < 5s 95% of the time in canary.

Open design questions (actionable):
1) Snapshot format: minimal KV pointers + small token window vs full token-indexed KV. Action: Jin to propose exact on-disk format and size estimate. Due: 2026-03-12.
2) Hotstore lifecycle: TTL defaults, eviction policies, cross-region considerations. Action: Marco to align with platform-engineering and hotstore owners and propose safe default (likely 2m TTL, soft-evict). Due: 2026-03-16.
3) Client-visible semantics for partial responses: do we return a structured error + partial output or abort? Action: Aisha to prototype client API extension (error-kind + resume_hint) and draft SDK changes. Due: 2026-03-19.
4) Security review for encrypted snapshots and KMS integration. Action: Samir to book S&P sync and list required threat-model tests. Due: 2026-03-11.
5) Billing/metrics implications: double-counting tokens for resumed sessions, how to charge for snapshot hotstore bytes. Action: Evan to create a short billing note + sample metrics instrumentation. Due: 2026-03-13.

Decisions made in this session (tentative):
- Adopt hybrid soft-preempt as default reclaim strategy for Dedicated pools with mixed-tier workloads. (Priya/Evan: +1)
- Default grace windows: urgent=2s, normal=10s, low=30s. These are tunable flags per pool.
- Snapshot heuristic: only snapshot when KV cache > 8MB or session_age > 30s when preempt hinted.
- Hotstore TTL default = 2 minutes for warm-candidate artifacts during rollout.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 0 (safety hooks, low risk - 2 weeks):
- Add preemption hint plumbing from scheduler -> node (signal only, no behavior change). Instrumentation for hint metrics. Owner: Priya.
Phase 1 (soft flush + early close batching - 3 weeks):
- Implement early flush of active generation windows on hint. Partial-response behavior behind feature flag. Owner: Jin.
Phase 2 (snapshot + resume basic & hotstore - 4 weeks):
- Minimal snapshot writer and hotstore TTL logic. Resume path that prefers hotstore blob. Owner: Marco + Samir.
Phase 3 (policy tuning + canary - 2 weeks):
- Run canary, collect telemetry, adjust grace timers and snapshot heuristics. Owner: Evan + Aisha.

Risks and mitigations:
- Hotstore overload: throttle snapshot attempts and add backpressure circuit in the node. Monitor hotstore queue depth.
- Incorrect resume causing divergence: keep ability to fall back to cold restart; log detailed diagnostics and add assert-level checks in canary.
- Billing surprises: early conversation with finance to set snapshot accounting and monitor sample traffic.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Jin: format proposal for snapshot payload (due 2026-03-12).
- Marco: hotstore lifecycle proposal + call with platform-engineering (due 2026-03-16).
- Aisha: SDK error/partial-response sketch and message format (due 2026-03-19).
- Samir: security threat-model checklist and schedule S&P review (due 2026-03-11).
- Evan: billing/metrics note + draft dashboards for key telemetry (due 2026-03-13).
- Priya: land preemption-hint plumbing PR (phase 0) and create the RFC stub that consolidates the above decisions. (Due 2026-03-09)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc captures an emergent design that prioritizes minimizing user-facing regressions while enabling priority-based reclaim. Please review the snapshot format proposal from Jin before the next meeting. We're intentionally conservative with defaults; the goal is to gather real-world data in canary rather than perfect the algorithm upfront.

Appendix: quick glossary
- soft-preempt hint: non-binding scheduler signal that asks a node to make room; node can use grace windows and checkpointing.
- hotstore: short-lived artifact store used to persist minimal resume blobs for warm resumption.
- warm-candidate: session marked as eligible for accelerated resume to reduce cold-start costs.

End of notes.
